newsitem.title: INDIA: SMIFS's technical outlook for Bombay share index.
newsitem.headline: SMIFS's technical outlook for Bombay share index.

text.p: This is the first in a series of opinion columns on the techncial outlook for the 3-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) sensitive index (sensex) by Dharmesh Rajdev, technical analyst at SMIFS Securities Ltd.

The sensex rallied last week and the retracement move did took the sensex approximately up to 38.2 percent retracement level of the fall (the fall which took the sensex down from 4130 to the low of 2930 i.e. a fall of 1200 points).
Thus 38.2 percent retracement level works out at 3388.4. During last week, the sensex touched the intraday high of 3344.67 and from there it came down sharply by nearly 100 points.
Hence the 38.2 percent retracement level did offer a strong resistance as expected.

The sensex during it's down move has shed about 29.95 percent of its value, when it touched the low of 2930. However important support and resistances were at 8 percent, 13 percent or 21 percent; suggesting values of 3799.6, 3593.1 or 3262.7. These percentage drops are Fibonnacci numbers and hence they have their due significance.

In the similar manner one can determine the future resistance levels of the current intermediate upmove. Taking the bottom of 2930 touched in early October 8, 13 & 21 percent levels work out of 3164.4, 3310.9 & 3545.30 respectively.
These are important support or resistance levels and closing above or below any level will take the sensex to the following or preceeding the target as the case may be.

During last week, the sensex opened at 3130.21 and rallied sharply for the announcement of market friendly credit policy to touch the high of 3344.67. Here massive profit booking forced the sensex to touch the low of 3230 before closing the week at 3250. In effect, the sensex gained 120 points during the week.

At the current juncture the fast weekly stochastic oscillator is at 49.19 with its trigger at 36.04, while the medium term slow weekly stochastic oscillator is placed at 20.04 with its trigger at 16.67.
Both these indicators are pointing upward and have crossed their trigger from below, indicating continuation of the current upmove in the market.

The eight weeks moving average is at 3263.29, while 25 weeks moving average is at 3549.60. The sensex has closed very near to eight weeks moving average and has crossed this average during its intra-weeks movement.
Once the sensex closes above this average, it is expected to inch towards 25 weeks moving average.
The nine weeks moving average on "highs" is a 3376.34 and nine Weeks moving average on "lows" is at 3225.91. Currently, sensex is trading in between these two bands.

Thus these are acting as resistance and support reply. However on daily basis these averages work out at 3211.09 and 3145.18. Thus a closing below these averages will be detrimental for the current upmove.
The 200 days moving average is at 3464.67. On the ascent this level will provide strong resistance to the sensex.
On the ascent sensex will face resistance at 3412-3385 band. While, on the descent support will emerge at 3217-3075 band.
(The opinions expressed in this article reflect the views of the author only. They should not be taken as reflecting the views of Reuters)
